comment: D-REL-14: the service readers' shared cases. tests/service-files.js (the node case "D-REL-14: the service readers")
and scripts/service_files.py (tests/test_service_files.py) each run every case: `service` is a Service.qml text,
`files` the code-behinds it may declare, by name. `expect.text` is the inline view, byte for byte; `expect.refusal`
is the kind both readers must refuse with; `declarations`, where given, the [file, qualifier] pairs in order.
Generated with every newline and CR written by code point, so the strings are exactly what they say.

cases.name: no declaration: the text as it is, and a forwarder-shaped line for a qualifier nobody declared stays
two code-behinds, each forwarder answered by its own, the declarations in their order
a CRLF checkout reads as the same view, every CR kept
a root comment directly above a forwarder stays on the root, above the moved block
a code-behind whose last line has no newline: its last function runs to the end of the file

files.Service-a.js:
// a

  function a(x) { return 2 }

cases.name: a declaration with a lowercase qualifier is refused
a declaration carrying a trailing comment is refused
an indented import of a script is refused
a declaration naming another directory is refused
an import of a script with no qualifier is refused
a file declared twice is refused
a qualifier declared twice is refused
a declared code-behind that is not there is refused
a forwarder whose call adds an argument is refused
a forwarder with its arguments swapped is refused
a forwarder spelled with other spacing is refused
a forwarder that calls another function is refused
a forwarder for a function its code-behind lacks is refused
two forwarders for one function are refused
a code-behind function no forwarder names is refused
a code-behind declaring one function twice is refused
a code-behind function with no closing brace is refused

files.Service-a.js:
function a(x) {
    return "}"

cases.name: a forwarder whose argument carries a default is refused: repeated in the call it is an assignment
a forwarder with a destructured argument is refused: repeated in the call it is a new object
a forwarder whose arguments are not its function's own is refused
a script imported in single quotes is refused, never read past
a code-behind statement outside every function is refused
a code-behind function at no indent is refused
a code-behind function spelled with a space before its parenthesis is refused
a code-behind header whose default holds parentheses is refused
a .pragma line in a code-behind is refused
blank lines holding spaces or a CR and loose // comments outside the functions read, and drop from the view
code after a code-behind function's closing brace on its line is refused: the harness reads a function from its header to its brace
a one-line code-behind function with a statement after its closing brace is refused

files.Service-a.js:
// a code-behind

  function a(x) { return 1 } Qt.callLater(function () { root.leak = 1 })

cases.name: a closing brace followed by spaces, a CR or a // comment reads, the comment kept in the view
a tree from before D-REL-5 imports its model as Model.js: that import is the model's, no code-behind, and the text is read as it is
the Model.js import beside a code-behind stays on the root while the code-behind is read in
a code-behind not named Service-<domain>.js is refused, however exactly it is declared and forwarded
a qualifier that is not its file's Service<Domain> is refused
a domain that is not lower-case letters and digits is refused: a capital
a domain holding a hyphen is refused: its qualifier could not be a name
a Model.js import on a text that imports Model.mjs is a script like any other, and refused, never kept unread
an ES module other than the model is refused: its forwarders would stay as root text and its body unread
the model imported in single quotes is refused: the one module import is exactly the model's
the model imported under another name is refused
a .import line in a code-behind is refused: a code-behind runs in the component's scope or not at all
the model's import and a code-behind named for its domain read: Service-<domain>.js as Service<Domain>, digits allowed
